conclusion: On this tested setup, nonempty bodyBytes replacement works, while zero-length bodyBytes and empty body text leave the original response intact. Safari and the HTTP export agree, so an Analyzer-only artifact does not explain these controlled cases.
bootstrapImplication: The response-stage bootstrap-empty mechanism cannot be accepted on this setup. This does not establish how YouTube would react to a genuine empty response.
limits: Observed on the reported device/QX version and public text fixtures; not a claim about every QX version or content type.
Request-stage echo completion and native binary fetch forwarding remain unverified.
